1. (Currently amended) A catheter system for delivering ultrasonic energy to a treatment site within a body lumen, the catheter comprising: a tubular body having a proximal end, a distal end and an energy delivery section positioned between the proximal end and the distal end; a plurality of ultrasound radiating members positioned within the energy delivery section, the plurality of ultrasound radiating members being allocated into at least three electrical groups comprising more than one ultrasound radiating member each; wherein the ultrasound radiating members of one electrical group are spatially interdigitated with the ultrasound radiating members of another electrical group __in a non-uniform spatial distribution__.

2. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, wherein the plurality of ultrasound radiating members are mounted on an inner core, wherein the inner core is configured for insertion into the tubular body, __and wherein the inner core comprises a non-conductive support structure__.

3. (Currently amended) The catheter system of Claim 1, further comprising at least one therapeutic compound delivery lumen that extends through the tubular body and terminates at least one outlet positioned in the energy delivery section, __wherein the therapeutic compound delivery lumen is positioned radially offset from the ultrasound radiating members__.

4. (Cancelled)

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Currently amended) A system for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the system comprising: a first ultrasound catheter and a second ultrasound catheter, each of the first and the second ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section having at least one ultrasound element, the tubular body also including at least one fluid delivery lumen, __each ultrasound catheter further comprising an elongate inner core supporting the at least one ultrasound element__; and a control system is connected to and configured to operate both the first and the second __ultrasound catheters__.

7. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 6, wherein the control system operates both the first and the second ultrasound catheters __in a coordinated manner with independent timing control for each catheter__.

8. (Currently amended) The system of Claim 7, wherein the control system is configured to independently control the ultrasound radiating members on the first and the second ultrasound catheters __with respect to frequency, amplitude, and phase parameters__.

9. (Currently amended) A method for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the method comprising: advancing an ultrasound catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen; advancing the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter to a treatment site in the patient's pulmonary artery; inflating a balloon on the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter; delivering a thrombolytic drug to the treatment site through the at least one fluid delivery lumen; and emitting ultrasonic energy __at a frequency greater than 100 kHz__ to thereby promote diffusion of the thrombolytic drug at the treatment site.

10. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 9, wherein delivering the thrombolytic drug and emitting ultrasonic energy are performed simultaneously, __and wherein the ultrasonic energy is modulated during drug delivery__.

11. (Currently amended) An ultrasound catheter for treating a patient having pulmonary embolism, the catheter comprising a tubular body having a proximal portion and a distal portion, the distal portion comprising an ultrasound energy delivery section comprising at least one ultrasound element and at least one fluid delivery lumen, the tubular body defining a guidewire lumen extending through the proximal portion and the ultrasound energy delivery section, __wherein the guidewire lumen is positioned eccentrically relative to the ultrasound energy delivery section__.

12. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, wherein the guidewire lumen extends through the at least one ultrasound element, __and wherein the ultrasound element is configured with a central aperture to accommodate the guidewire lumen__.

13. (Currently amended) The ultrasound catheter of Claim 11, further comprising at least one balloon positioned at the distal portion of the ultrasound catheter, __wherein the balloon is positioned proximal to the ultrasound energy delivery section__.
